raw_response.description: A walking mountain whose upper hide is a fused sheet of mirror-bright, ablative plate — nothing soft is ever turned toward the sun. Every opening it has, every soft fold of skin, every sense organ, lives instead on its lower, shaded flank, permanently turned away from the light. It moves at the pace of a shadow on a sundial, and the shade it throws is the coolest, busiest ground for a hundred kilometres in any direction. Nothing here has ever needed to chase anything; the giant simply keeps walking, and whatever needs shade learns to walk with it.
